gp.heading: Gross Profit:
gp.text: Gross profit as a percentage of sales decreased 0.5% for 2025 as compared to 2024 driven by lower volumes partially offset by effective cost management. The year ended December 31, 2025 includes a last-in, first-out (“LIFO”) charge of $17,956, which is primarily due to rising input costs. This compares with a LIFO benefit of $9,313 in 2024.

oi.heading: Operating Income:
oi.text: Operating income as a percentage of sales was 17.0% in 2025 as compared to 15.9% in 2024. Excluding special items, Operating income as a percentage of sales was 17.6% for both 2025 and 2024. Refer to explanations above for additional details. Also refer to Non-GAAP Financial Measures for a reconciliation of Adjusted operating income.

rd.text: The Company invests in the research and development of its solutions in order to continue its market leading product offering and improve the quality, productivity and sustainability of its solutions. The Company believes its significant investment in research and development, its highly trained technical sales force and its extensive distributor network provide a competitive advantage in the marketplace.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: The Company is not dependent on a single customer or a few customers and no individual customer currently accounts for more than ten percent of total Net sales.
No individual customer comprised more than 10% of the Company’s total revenues in 2025, 2024 or 2023.
Our operations depend on maintaining a skilled workforce, and any interruption in our workforce could negatively impact our results of operations and financial condition.
Our future success will also depend on our ability to identify, attract and retain highly qualified managerial and technical (including research and development) personnel.

We rely upon patent, trademark, copyright and trade secret laws in the United States and similar laws in foreign countries, as well as agreements with our employees, customers, suppliers and other third parties, to establish and maintain our intellectual property rights.
The Company’s primary sources of liquidity are operating cash flows and revolving credit facilities.
Fair value estimates are based on a series of judgments about future events and uncertainties and rely on estimates and assumptions.
The accounting for gains and losses resulting from changes in fair value depends on the use of the derivative and whether it is designated and qualifies for hedge accounting.
